summary: The tariff picture changed since earlier runs: IEEPA duties ended in Feb 2026, a 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 24, and China-origin goods now pay MFN + original Section 301 (25% Lists 1-3, 7.5% List 4A) + a new 12.5% Section 301 forced-labor tariff, so all duty rates here use that stack. Fibermaxxing, creatine, magnesium, K-beauty and supplements dominate current TikTok Shop and Google signals, and Q4 cozy/gifting items are in season. Evidence quality is mixed: Amazon Movers & Shakers and Reddit could not be fetched, and most unit costs are estimates from listing ranges, not supplier quotes.
changes_vs_last_run: Carried over from the 2026-10-26 run: pet enrichment bundle, rosemary hair oil kit, toothpaste tablets, hard water shower filter, creatine gummies, magnesium gummies, neck wrap gift set. Duty rates were re-based to the post-IEEPA stack (12.5% Section 301 + Section 301 list rate where applicable); I did not re-derive the previous run's scores, so no score-move comparisons are claimed. New entrants this week: tallow balm, heatless curl set, electrolyte sticks, fiber gummies, quiet cat fountain, dog multivitamin chews, dog stroller, car organizer bundle, 3-in-1 charging station, wax warmer bundle, insulated tumbler, fleece leggings, kids craft kit, LED red light mask, humidifier, rechargeable hand warmers, pickleball set, wearable blanket hoodie, acupressure mat set, calming pet bed, gua sha set. Three new kills added (research peptides, designer-dupe fragrances, compounded GLP-1 drops).

candidates.name: Pet enrichment bundle: silicone lick mat + fabric snuffle mat + slow feeder bowl
candidates.angle: Bundle three products with thicker food-grade silicone, stronger suction and a printed enrichment guide, against single-item listings with weak suction.
candidates.regulatory_notes: Pet product, no FDA premarket approval. Silicone should be food-grade (FDA 21 CFR 177.2600) with a test report; avoid health claims such as 'treats anxiety'. No FCC/CPSIA.
candidates.notes: Unit cost is a blend of Alibaba-aggregator lick mat listings ($0.93-$4.42, MOQs 10-1440) plus an assumed snuffle mat and feeder; no supplier quote. Duty assumes HTS 3924.90 on Section 301 List 3: 3.4% MFN + 25% + 12.5%; HTS not verified. Freight is a sea LCL guess at about $0.30-0.80/kg. Fulfill fee is a conservative large-standard guess. Confidence in demand: medium; confidence in cost: low-medium.

candidates.name: Rosemary hair oil (2 oz) + silicone scalp massager kit, US contract-filled
candidates.angle: Lighter, faster-absorbing formula with a leak-proof dropper and a bundled massager, positioned as scalp care and not hair-regrowth.
candidates.regulatory_notes: Cosmetic under MoCRA: facility registration and product listing via the contract manufacturer and responsible person (small-business exemption under $1M average cosmetic sales has limits, so verify on fda.gov). Ingredient labeling, safety substantiation, adverse event records. Do NOT claim hair growth or treating hair loss; that makes it an unapproved drug.
candidates.notes: Cost is a guess: a Beautetrade private-label rosemary biotin shampoo listing shows $2-$10 FOB at MOQ 500, and I found no oil-specific quote. Duty is blended: oil is US-made (0%), massager imported (assumed about 40% duty on a small share of cost). Orders per customer 1.8 is conservative because most customers do not reorder. Revenue per customer is about $50. Market is crowded with brands.

candidates.name: Toothpaste tablets, 3-month supply in refill pouch (fluoride-free)
candidates.angle: Moisture-proof refill pouch, better mint flavor and a clear 3-month subscription offer, aimed at eco-minded buyers.
candidates.regulatory_notes: A fluoride-free tablet is a cosmetic (MoCRA labeling/listing). Adding fluoride and an anticavity claim makes it an OTC drug under the FDA monograph, which needs drug facility registration and an OTC label. Avoid claims such as 'prevents cavities' or 'remineralizes'.
candidates.notes: Assumes US contract manufacture (0% duty). If made in Asia, add the China stack (3304/3306 lines are not verified). Market-size estimates vary widely ($40M-$151M global), so demand is uncertain. Reorder 2.0 per year assumes a 3-month supply, with some repurchase.

candidates.name: Hard water shower filter head, 15-stage vitamin C/KDF, with 2 spare cartridges
candidates.angle: Include two spare cartridges and a pressure-boost design, with honest chlorine and hard-water claims, in the upfront price.
candidates.regulatory_notes: Avoid health claims. Water-treatment claims on the label may trigger state rules and NSF/ANSI expectations; FTC substantiation applies. Amazon may require test reports for filter claims. No FCC.
candidates.notes: Cost is a guess from typical filter head listings. Duty assumes HTS about 8421.21 or 3924 on List 3 or similar: about 25% + 12.5% + a few % MFN, not verified. ASINSight shows the top 3 products hold 44.6% of click share and a top-10 average price of $30.17, so the $45 price is above market and has to be justified by the spare cartridges. Exploding Topics lists 40.5K volume.

candidates.name: Creatine monohydrate gummies, 60 count, US contract-manufactured
candidates.angle: Clinical dose (3-5 g) per serving with third-party testing and lot COAs, against gummies that under-dose.
candidates.regulatory_notes: Dietary supplement under DSHEA: cGMP contract manufacturer, Supplement Facts panel, structure/function claims with the FDA disclaimer, notify FDA within 30 days of marketing a claim. No disease claims. Amazon requires third-party testing for supplements and category approval.
candidates.notes: Spate reports creatine gummies up 101% YoY and Bupa/Google data show rising creatine interest, mostly UK women. Cost is an estimate: a true 3-5 g dose per gummy-serving is expensive, and I found no quote. Reorder 1.7 is conservative.

candidates.name: Magnesium glycinate gummies, 60 count, US contract-manufactured
candidates.angle: Disclose elemental magnesium per serving, use low sugar, and differentiate on a sleep or stress routine bundle.
candidates.regulatory_notes: Dietary supplement rules as above (cGMP, Supplement Facts, structure/function claims only, third-party testing for Amazon).
candidates.notes: Spate: magnesium glycinate +33.6% YoY, magnesium gummies forecast +35.1%. The #2 US TikTok Shop item in Q2 2026 was Toplux Magnesium at $14.23M, so the category is heavily contested. Cost is an estimate.

candidates.name: Microwavable weighted neck wrap + eye mask gift set
candidates.angle: Washable cover, sealed inner liner and a gift box, sold for Q4 gifting.
candidates.regulatory_notes: Textile labeling (FTC Textile Act/care labels). Not a medical device unless therapeutic claims are made; avoid pain-relief claims. Flammability for fabrics.
candidates.notes: Duty is a conservative estimate for textile articles (about 7.5% or 25% Section 301 + 12.5% + MFN); HTS not verified. Seasonal, so trend is capped at 5. Revenue per customer is about $38, borderline against the $40 target.

candidates.name: Whipped beef tallow and honey balm, 2 oz, US contract-made
candidates.angle: Odor-neutral, non-greasy whipped texture, sealed jar and a heat-stable formula, aimed at a men's or sensitive-skin niche.
candidates.regulatory_notes: Cosmetic under MoCRA (registration/listing via the manufacturer, ingredient labeling, adverse event records). No treatment claims for eczema or acne. Animal-derived ingredient sourcing documentation advisable.
candidates.notes: ASINSight: leaders sell about 20,000 units/month at $19.99-$27.97; URQT sells about 3,000 at $9.99. Weekly 'beef tallow' searches include cooking, so they overstate skincare demand. Spike-fade risk, so trend 5. Revenue per customer is about $41, borderline.

candidates.name: Heatless curl set deluxe: satin curling rod, bonnet, scrunchies, eye mask
candidates.angle: Firmer, longer-lasting rod and a larger-size option for thick hair, bundled with an eye mask for a higher order value.
candidates.regulatory_notes: Textile labeling; no other beyond standard rules.
candidates.notes: Future Market Insights: market $232M in 2026; Kitsch's top item sells about 10K/month per ASINSight, so a strong incumbent. Revenue per customer is about $38, just under the $40 target. Duty is an estimate for textile/hair accessory lines.

candidates.name: Electrolyte hydration powder sticks, 30 count, sugar-free, US-made
candidates.angle: A niche flavor or use-case line (e.g., pregnancy-friendly or kids) with a lower sodium taste profile.
candidates.regulatory_notes: Dietary supplement or conventional food depending on format and claims; FDA labeling, cGMP contract manufacturer; no disease claims. Amazon grocery/supplement approvals may apply.
candidates.notes: Recharge data: electrolyte subscription revenue up 37% YoY, but new-subscriber signups flat; supplement churn 5-8% per month. Giants dominate (low competition_score). Reorder 2.2 is deliberately conservative.

candidates.name: Prebiotic fiber gummies, 60 count, US contract-manufactured
candidates.angle: Real fiber dose per serving with a diverse-fiber blend, since coverage says 'fiber diversity' is the 2026 focus.
candidates.regulatory_notes: Dietary supplement: cGMP, Supplement Facts, structure/function claims only (avoid claims about treating constipation or IBS).
candidates.notes: Fibermaxxing was heavily covered in 2026 (CNN, Bloomberg, Circana), but one source says it is fading into 'fiber diversity'; I found no supplement-specific sales data. Gummies hold limited fiber per piece, which limits the dose. Cost is a guess.

candidates.name: Quiet stainless-steel cat water fountain with 4 spare filters
fixable_complaints: pump buzzes when water is low
candidates.angle: Low-water cutoff, easy-access pump and filters bundled in the box, against noisy, hard-to-clean competitors.
candidates.regulatory_notes: Low-voltage adapter: UL/ETL listing and FCC Part 15 declaration for the electronics; materials should be food-contact safe. Amazon may require safety documents.
candidates.notes: Complaint evidence comes from Chewy/zooplus reviews and an eufy support page. I found no market-size or growth data, so trend 6 is a judgment. Duty estimate assumes about 8413/3924 lines at 25% + 12.5% + MFN; not verified. Unit cost is a guess.

candidates.name: Dog multivitamin soft chews, 90 count, US contract-manufactured
candidates.angle: Palatable soft chew with NASC-style quality seal and transparent sourcing.
candidates.regulatory_notes: Animal supplement: FDA CVM and state feed-control (AAFCO model) labeling, no disease-treatment claims; NASC seal optional. Registrations may be needed in several states.
candidates.notes: Exploding Topics lists dog vitamins at +150% (Oct 17, 2026 update). No sales data found. Cost is a guess; pet supplement contract manufacturing quotes were not found.

candidates.name: Foldable dog stroller for small dogs
candidates.angle: Sturdier frame and one-hand fold, with a clear weight limit.
candidates.regulatory_notes: No special federal rules for pet strollers; avoid child-stroller claims (CPSC). Product liability insurance advised.
candidates.notes: Exploding Topics +178% (Oct 2026). Bulky, so freight and FBA fees are large; margin is likely thin. Fulfill fee and freight are rough guesses; duty assumed about 8716/8715-type line, not verified. Low confidence.

candidates.name: Car organizer bundle: backseat organizer + collapsible trunk organizer
candidates.angle: Rigid inner panels and a matched two-piece set at a bundle price.
candidates.regulatory_notes: None beyond standard rules.
candidates.notes: Cohley: median top-10 seller in the category has about 8,270 reviews; the Helteko backseat organizer has 11K+ reviews, so hard to beat. Complaint evidence is thin: I found no review analysis. Costs are guesses.

candidates.name: 3-in-1 foldable Qi2 magnetic wireless charging station
candidates.angle: Include a 30W adapter and a stronger magnet alignment, with heat-managed charging.
candidates.regulatory_notes: FCC equipment authorization (intentional radiator, Part 15), UL/ETL safety for the charger, Qi certification for the logo; Li-ion not inside, so no battery shipping rule; ENERGY STAR/DoE external power supply efficiency rules for the adapter.
candidates.notes: FastMoss/HyperSKU show Computers & Office as the fastest-growing Q4 category (+38.6% YoY). Duty guess is 25% + 12.5% (8504.40 List status not verified). Revenue per customer equals price ($39), just under $40. Cost is a guess.

candidates.name: Wax melt warmer lamp + 12 wax melts bundle
candidates.angle: Dimmable lamp with a replaceable bulb and refill subscription for melts.
candidates.regulatory_notes: UL/ETL listing for the electric warmer; candle/wax labeling and CPSC flammability considerations; fragrance allergen labeling is advisable.
candidates.notes: Seasonal Q4 item per HyperSKU; trend capped at 4. Melts could be a repeat purchase, which is why orders are 1.4 (a guess). Costs are guesses.

candidates.name: 40 oz insulated tumbler with handle and straw, 2 lids
candidates.angle: Leak-proof lid and durable powder coat; a niche color drop to differentiate.
candidates.regulatory_notes: Food-contact compliance (FDA, California Prop 65 for lead in solder/coatings); test report advised. Avoid brand-lookalike trade dress.
candidates.notes: Printful and Bonfire list drinkware as a top 2026 category, but the market is saturated with big brands. Duty guess uses 9617 vacuum flask (7% MFN) + 25% + 12.5%; unverified. Revenue per customer is about $41.

candidates.name: Fleece-lined thermal leggings 2-pack
candidates.angle: Accurate size chart, opaque fabric and extended sizes.
candidates.regulatory_notes: Textile fiber, care and country-of-origin labeling; flammability (16 CFR 1610). Not a children's item unless sized as such.
candidates.notes: HyperSKU: leggings with over half of lifetime sales in Q4. Duty uses about 14.9% MFN (knit apparel) + 7.5% List 4A + 12.5% is nearer 0.35; unverified. Returns on sizing will hurt margin and are not modeled. Strongly seasonal.

candidates.name: Kids DIY craft mega kit (bracelets and gem art), 3 projects
candidates.angle: Pre-counted pieces, clear picture instructions and a reusable storage box.
candidates.regulatory_notes: Children's product: CPSIA third-party testing at a CPSC-accepted lab, Children's Product Certificate, ASTM F963, tracking labels, small-parts warning for ages under 3 / choking hazard labels, lead and phthalate limits. Amazon requires the CPC.
candidates.notes: Toys & Hobbies Q4 premium is 3.0x per HyperSKU (+7.9% YoY). Testing cost (a few hundred to over $1K per SKU) is not in unit_cost. Duty is an estimate.

candidates.name: LED red light therapy face mask (consumer wearable)
candidates.angle: Comfortable fit with a long cord or a safe battery pack, plus a clear no-medical-claims positioning.
candidates.regulatory_notes: LED masks making acne or wrinkle claims are regulated as FDA Class II devices (510(k) clearance); a seller either needs clearance or must avoid such claims. Also FCC Part 15, IEC 62471 eye safety, UL, and lithium battery rules (UN38.3) if battery-powered. Amazon may gate the category.
candidates.notes: Meetglimpse claims red-light search interest +59% over the past year (undated); a JMIR study notes a TikTok-driven wave. Cost is a guess. Regulatory burden and high CPC make this a high-risk pick. Duty is an estimate (8543 or 9018 line unverified).

candidates.name: 4L top-fill cool mist humidifier with essential oil tray
candidates.angle: Wide-mouth, dishwasher-safe tank and a quiet motor, against mold and leak complaints.
candidates.regulatory_notes: UL/ETL listing, FCC for any electronic controls, CPSC watch on humidifier recalls; no health claims (e.g., 'relieves congestion').
candidates.notes: Humidifiers are on the HyperSKU/Fastlane lists; seasonal winter demand. Competition is heavy with big brands. Duty guess about 4.2% MFN + 25% + 12.5%; unverified. Revenue per customer equals price.

candidates.name: Rechargeable magnetic hand warmers, 2-pack
candidates.angle: Slim form with a certified battery and an auto shutoff, against bulky models that drain quickly.
candidates.regulatory_notes: Lithium battery: UN38.3 test report, UL 2054/UL 62133 recommended, hazmat shipping rules (Class 9, UN3481), FCC for any electronics. CPSC has recalled over 1.5 million rechargeable warmers for fire and burn risks, so recall exposure is real. Amazon requires battery documents.
candidates.notes: Complaints from BestReviews and an Alibaba review analysis; recalls reported by news outlets. Seasonal, trend 4. Costs are guesses; FBA hazmat fees may be higher than the fulfill_fee used.

candidates.name: Pickleball starter set: 2 paddles, 4 balls, carry bag
candidates.angle: USAPA-approved paddles with a better bag at the same price as the leading set.
candidates.regulatory_notes: None beyond standard rules; USA Pickleball approval list is optional but matters to serious buyers.
candidates.notes: SFIA via a 2026 summary: 24.3M US players in 2025, +22.8% YoY, but growth is slowing. ASINSight: the leading paddle set sells about 10K/month, down 40% month over month, top-10 average price $57.68. Duty guess about 25% + 12.5%; HTS unverified.

candidates.name: Wearable blanket hoodie, oversized sherpa fleece
candidates.angle: Two sizes and a better-quality sherpa lining, sold as a gift.
candidates.regulatory_notes: Textile and care labeling; flammability for apparel (16 CFR 1610). Children's sizes would need CPSIA.
candidates.notes: Cozy home/oversized hoodie are on the Q4 lists (HyperSKU, Fastlane). Bulky, so freight and fees are higher. Strong seasonality; duty is an estimate.

candidates.name: Acupressure mat and neck pillow set
candidates.angle: Gentler spike pattern, a thicker foam core and a starter guide.
candidates.regulatory_notes: Avoid pain-relief claims, which can bring FDA device scrutiny. Textile labeling applies.
candidates.notes: Evidence is weak: only general wellness/yoga accessory mentions in trend lists. Revenue per customer is about $40. Costs are guesses.

candidates.name: Orthopedic calming donut pet bed, washable, medium
candidates.angle: Higher-density fill, non-slip base and a cover that survives the wash.
candidates.regulatory_notes: State stuffed-article/bedding labeling (e.g., law tags) may apply; Prop 65. Avoid anxiety-treatment claims.
candidates.notes: Pet beds appear on HyperSKU's Q4 list; APPA shows steady pet spending growth ($158B in 2025). No bed-specific sales data was found. Costs are guesses.

candidates.name: Gua sha, ice roller and facial massage gift set
candidates.angle: Real stone with a quality gift box, sold for Q4 gifting.
candidates.regulatory_notes: Non-electric tool, standard consumer rules. Avoid medical claims; if bundled with serums, the serum falls under MoCRA.
candidates.notes: Facial tools were noted as a Q4 TikTok Shop category (a beauty wand earned over half its lifetime sales in Q4 2025). Revenue per customer is about $35, below $40, so it does not clearly meet the target. Duty is an estimate.

candidates.name: Research-use-only peptides (BPC-157 and similar) sold as vials
candidates.kill_reason: Unapproved drugs: 'research use only' labeling gives no legal defense for marketing to consumers and FDA has no approved BPC-157 product.
candidates.angle: n/a
candidates.regulatory_notes: Not sellable to US consumers.
candidates.notes: Law-firm and telehealth sources agree; the FDA status of compounding details conflicts across sources, but the consumer-sale conclusion does not.

candidates.name: Designer-brand 'dupe' perfumes using brand names or trade dress
candidates.kill_reason: Counterfeit or trademark-infringing goods when brand names or look-alike packaging are used.
candidates.angle: n/a
candidates.regulatory_notes: Original-scent fragrances are legal under MoCRA; only the branded-dupe version is killed.
candidates.notes: Dupe culture drives discovery per Fastlane, but names or trade dress of the original make it infringing.

candidates.name: Compounded or 'GLP-1' semaglutide drops and sprays sold online
candidates.kill_reason: Unapproved drug marketed as a supplement; cannot be legally sold to consumers.
candidates.angle: n/a
candidates.regulatory_notes: Not sellable as described.
